topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the series and establishes the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation, environmental exposures, and research methodologies.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Causation: Genetics, Chance, and Environmental Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core drivers of cancer etiology by examining the interplay between intrinsic random mutations, inherited predispositions, lifestyle factors, and geographic epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis and the Burkitt Lymphoma Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how biological agents cause cancer, detailing the specific discovery and multi-step oncogenic mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma involving Epstein-Barr virus and malaria.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail various dietary, chemical, and environmental carcinogens and the molecular pathways—including xenobiotic metabolism and DNA adduct formation—by which they damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility Contexts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic promotional mechanisms of cancer, distinguishing initiators from promoters and assessing how chronic inflammation and host developmental timing permit tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methodologies used to evaluate carcinogens, ranging from mutational signature analysis and biobank epidemiology to in vivo rodent assays and the in vitro Ames test.

topics.label: Conclusion and Everyday Risk Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the core themes of the lecture and discusses how individuals and society balance exposure risks against practical benefits.
